title: WhaleSpotter thermal-camera AI on a Coast Guard station at Angel Island starts alerting San Francisco Bay mariners and the Vessel Traffic Service to gray whales
summary: WhaleSpotter’s thermal AI and human review feed whale alerts to San Francisco Bay mariners; independent reporters documented deployment and Coast Guard use, without a measured decline in strikes.
account: UC Santa Barbara announced the San Francisco Bay WhaleSpotter system on May 19, 2026. Its first thermal camera was on Angel Island. AI flags whale heat signatures, a marine-mammal specialist checks them, and confirmed detections appear on Whale Safe for mariners and the Coast Guard’s Vessel Traffic Service. IEEE Spectrum attended the launch and reported that the system had logged 6,600 detections in about a week and a half. These were repeated detections, not 6,600 individual whales. Bay Nature later visited the traffic service and described its dedicated Whale Safe screen, near-daily detections, radio guidance to captains, and a second camera on the ferry Lyra. That reporting establishes operational use. The sources do not measure a reduction in strikes or link a particular alert to a documented avoided collision.
purpose: The network was built to detect whales in the bay around the clock and alert vessels so they can slow or alter course.
system: FLIR thermal cameras with WhaleSpotter AI detection, human verification and Whale Safe alert mapping
developer: WhaleSpotter (detection AI) with UC Santa Barbara's Benioff Ocean Science Laboratory
deployer: Benioff Ocean Science Laboratory with the U.S. Coast Guard Vessel Traffic Service and The Marine Mammal Center
taxonomy_note: Launch only; the aim is whale conservation, which Trustible's description reaches only as “improved environment”.

ratings.reason: The sources document detections and operational alerts, but no measured change in strikes or independently documented avoided collision.
No outcome for ferry or shipping operators is documented.

ai_role.statement: AI detects candidate whale signatures in thermal imagery. Human specialists verify them before alerts reach mariners. IEEE Spectrum adds an early detection count and the developer’s explanation of why human review remains necessary. Bay Nature independently observed the Coast Guard workflow. Neither report independently estimates the system’s effect on whale survival.

fields.account: UC Santa Barbara announced the San Francisco Bay WhaleSpotter system on May 19, 2026. Its first thermal camera was on Angel Island. AI flags whale heat signatures, a marine-mammal specialist checks them, and confirmed detections appear on Whale Safe for mariners and the Coast Guard’s Vessel Traffic Service. IEEE Spectrum attended the launch and reported that the system had logged 6,600 detections in about a week and a half. These were repeated detections, not 6,600 individual whales. Bay Nature later visited the traffic service and described its dedicated Whale Safe screen, near-daily detections, radio guidance to captains, and a second camera on the ferry Lyra. That reporting establishes operational use. The sources do not measure a reduction in strikes or link a particular alert to a documented avoided collision.

fields.headline: WhaleSpotter thermal AI starts whale alerts in San Francisco Bay

provenance.basis: Preserved from the existing AIBD record; external sources were not rechecked.

value.role: SHA-256 of normalized current case data

provenance.basis: Deterministic content version of the updated case record.

fields.account: UC Santa Barbara announced the San Francisco Bay WhaleSpotter system on May 19, 2026. Its first thermal camera was on Angel Island. AI flags whale heat signatures, a marine-mammal specialist checks them, and confirmed detections appear on Whale Safe for mariners and the Coast Guard’s Vessel Traffic Service. IEEE Spectrum attended the launch and reported that the system had logged 6,600 detections in about a week and a half. These were repeated detections, not 6,600 individual whales. Bay Nature later visited the traffic service and described its dedicated Whale Safe screen, near-daily detections, radio guidance to captains, and a second camera on the ferry Lyra. That reporting establishes operational use. The sources do not measure a reduction in strikes or link a particular alert to a documented avoided collision.

produced_by: A fixed vantage point over a whale-vessel overlap hotspot
Thermal cameras able to see blows at several nautical miles
Human review of each AI detection before alerting
A Vessel Traffic Service willing to relay alerts by radio
must_hold: Whales continue to enter the bay in the detection footprint
Mariners and ferry operators act on posted detections
Funding sustains camera nodes and specialist review

display.answer: Thermal cameras observed an area used by whales and vessels. People reviewed each AI detection before Vessel Traffic Service operators relayed alerts by radio.
